calib_controls / calib_standards / control_reference: estimates and expected values for controls and calibrators (0.7.0)

Source: calib_points_SPEC.md

Goal. Store, for every control well and every calibrator (standard-curve point), the same modelled estimates calib_samples holds for test samples: back-calculated concentration, precision (pcov), precision gate, censoring, and posterior or predictive quantiles. This lets I-SPI and exports read them directly instead of recomputing them, and supports replicate linearity, standard-source bridging, batch and multisite normalization, and long-term control and calibrator tracking within and across studies.

Ownership. The schema is defined here (R/calib_schema.sql, mirrored by point_estimates_contract()); curveRfreq and curveRbayes produce the estimates; curveRcore adds precision gates, censoring and standard recovery; the i-spi-compute worker writes the rows; I-SPI reads them. A test keeps the DDL and the contract in sync.

Decisions

  1. Estimates never change a fit. Both engines back-calculate points after the curve is fitted (predict_samples_freq(), predict_samples_bayes()). Controls and standards go through the same step, so fitted curves, parameters and existing calib_samples rows are unchanged.
  2. Controls get their own table, calib_controls, one row per (curve_id, method, well). A separate table keeps controls out of everything that reads calib_samples, in particular the precision-weight fits.
  3. A control is estimated through every curve it can be read on: the same matching as test samples (plate, nominal sample dilution, antigen, feature, wavelength; every standard source), via the worker’s new control_for_fit view.
  4. Masked controls are estimated too, with included = FALSE, exclusion_reason = 'masked' and the mask_reason. (Masked test samples are still dropped before estimation, unchanged.)
  5. calib_standards keeps its key and its existing columns; the estimate columns are added as nullable columns (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS). Rows written before 0.7.0 keep NULL estimates until the curve is refitted.
  6. Standards know their true value, so they carry two things samples cannot:
    • recovery_pct = 100 x estimated / nominal concentration (both at the dilution the point was run at, i.e. 10^(predicted_log10_concentration - log10_concentration)).
    • a bias-aware pcov_rmse: the CV of the root-mean-square error, sqrt(se^2 + bias^2), where bias is the log10 difference between the estimate and the nominal value. For samples and controls bias is unknown and pcov_rmse = pcov, as before.
  7. A standard that entered the fit is checked against a curve it helped shape, so its recovery is optimistic. included says which points were in the fit; masked standards are independent checks. Readers should show this.
  8. For a standard, final_concentration = estimate x dilution is that point’s estimate of the stock concentration. Across points, sources and plates it is the quantity to compare when bridging standard sources.
  9. Expected (nominal) values of controls are not stored with the estimates. calib_controls.concentration / log10_concentration are present for symmetry with calib_standards and stay NULL. Expected values live in control_reference and are joined at read time by the calib_controls_qc view, because they are assigned and revised independently of fitting (see Control reference values).
  10. Same vocabularies as calib_samples: censor_class, censor_type, pcov_gate_class carry the same CHECK constraints.

Columns

calib_controls (new): curve_id, method, well, sampleid, source, dilution, included, exclusion_reason, mask_reason, concentration, log10_concentration, response_model, assay_response_raw, predicted_concentration, predicted_log10_concentration, final_concentration, se_concentration, pcov, pcov_rmse, pcov_pass, pcov_gate_class, censor_class, censor_type, censor_lower, censor_upper, conc_q_lo, conc_q_med, conc_q_hi, p_below_lloq, p_above_uloq, p_below_cutoff, frac_draws_below_a, frac_draws_above_d, job_id, created_at. Key (curve_id, method, well); FK curve_id -> curve_lookup ON DELETE CASCADE.

calib_standards (added): predicted_concentration, predicted_log10_concentration, final_concentration, se_concentration, pcov, pcov_rmse, pcov_pass, pcov_gate_class, censor_class, censor_type, censor_lower, censor_upper, conc_q_lo, conc_q_med, conc_q_hi, p_below_lloq, p_above_uloq, p_below_cutoff, frac_draws_below_a, frac_draws_above_d, recovery_pct.

Per-column meaning: point_estimates_contract().

Result object (engines -> worker)

A fitted calibration_result may carry two new data frames beside $samples:

  • $controls: the control rows handed to the engine, with the sample estimate columns added.
  • $standard_estimates: the standard rows (included and masked), with the same estimate columns added. concentration is the x value the fit used (log10 when is_log_independent).

classify_pcov_gates_multiplate() and classify_censoring_multiplate() now process $samples, $controls and $standard_estimates identically. add_standard_recovery_multiplate() adds recovery_pct and the bias-aware pcov_rmse to $standard_estimates. A result without the new slots is handled exactly as before.

Rollout

  1. curveRcore 0.7.0: this contract, DDL, gating/censoring over all point types, standard recovery, control_reference + calib_controls_qc, the backfill function, and the release-manifest pieces (schema_version, calib_run.manifest, release_manifest()).
  2. curveRfreq / curveRbayes 0.6.0: controls = argument and an estimate_standards option (defaults leave output unchanged).
  3. i-spi-compute migration 011 (same statements as the 0.7.0 DDL additions, plus the control_for_fit view) and worker 1.1.0. Applied before the new worker starts; additive only, no downtime.
  4. One-off backfill (below) of every curve fitted before 0.7.0.
  5. I-SPI 1.1.0: clone/delete include calib_controls (and the control_reference rows of a cloned study); Replicate Linearity and exports read only stored estimates. Because of the backfill there is no in-app fallback computation.

Backfill of curves fitted before 0.7.0

estimate_points_from_stored() rebuilds every estimate column for a set of points read on one stored curve, from what the database already holds; nothing is refitted and existing fit rows are not touched. A one-off runner in i-spi-compute (with migration 011) reads, per (curve, method): the best model’s calib_param rows (including sigma_resid for frequentist fits), calib_grid, calib_diagnostics, curve-scope calib_draws (and, for Bayesian fits, the population sigma_obs, nu, log_sigma0, log_sigma_slope draws and the noise model recorded in calib_run.params). It then updates the calib_standards rows (response: response_model; nominal: log10_concentration) and inserts calib_controls rows (response: the raw control response, log-transformed as the fit was) with job_id = 'backfill-0.7.0'.

How close the result is to what the engine would have stored (checked against curveRfreq 0.5.1 and curveRbayes 0.5.1 on bead_assay_example, 20 samples):

Column Frequentist Bayesian
point estimate identical (inverse at the estimates) median of the inverted draws: within the engine’s own run-to-run Monte Carlo spread; inverse at the stored estimates when no draws are stored
se, pcov stored profile: within 0.1%; outside the profile, from the draws: within 0.3% SD of the inverted draws with the fitted noise: within the engine’s run-to-run spread; the stored profile when no draws are stored
gate, censoring identical (20/20) identical (20/20)
quantiles, probabilities same parameter draws with fresh noise draws: equal in distribution same

Without stored draws (fits before curveRfreq 0.5.0, or Bayesian fits without persist_draws) the quantile and probability columns stay NULL, as they are in calib_samples for those fits.

Control reference values

control_reference (owned by I-SPI; the engines never read it): one row per expected value and validity period of a control (control_source = calib_controls.source), lot, antigen and feature, within a project and optionally one study ('__none__' = project-wide / every feature). Values are at stock (dilution 1), the scale of calib_controls.final_concentration: expected_conc, expected_sd, lower_limit, upper_limit, units, basis (certificate, assigned, historical), valid_from (default -infinity), valid_to (NULL = still in force), assigned_by, assigned_at, note. A changed value is a new row with a new valid_from, and the old row is closed with valid_to, so history is kept.

calib_controls_qc joins each control estimate to the value in force on the plate’s acquisition date (xmap_header), preferring a study-specific over a project-wide value and a feature-specific over an every-feature value, and adds recovery_pct = 100 * final_concentration / expected_conc, z_score = (final_concentration - expected_conc) / expected_sd and within_limits. Westgard rules need the sequence of runs and are applied by I-SPI over this view.

Integration in I-SPI (after 1.1.0): an editor for values with a “suggest from history” action (mean and SD of stored estimates over chosen runs, saved only when a person accepts it), Levey-Jennings charts per control, antigen and standard source within and across studies, normalization factors, and export columns.

Release manifest

madi_results.schema_version records each schema component and version applied (calib_schema = calib_schema_version(), written by calib_schema.sql itself). calib_run.manifest (jsonb) holds, per job, the manifest the worker ran under: release_manifest() (R, curveR package versions, CmdStan, calib schema version, renv lock MD5) plus the worker’s component name, image version and commit, serialised with manifest_json(). NULL for jobs run before 0.7.0.
